subtopics.title: Economic Systems and the Four Factors

questions.question: Economic systems differ fundamentally by:
options: WHO answers the three questions — prices in the free market, planners in the planned economy, both in the mixed

questions.question: South Africa is called DUALISTIC because:
options: A first-world financial and industrial economy operates BESIDE a large informal and subsistence economy

questions.question: The four factors earn, in order — natural resources, labour, capital, entrepreneurship:
Profit is called the RESIDUAL because it is:
options: Whatever REMAINS after rent, wages and interest are paid — possibly negative, which is why it rewards risk

subtopics.title: Measuring and Mapping the Economy — Aggregates, Sectors and Infrastructure

questions.question: The three methods of measuring GDP are:
options: PRODUCTION summing value added, INCOME summing factor earnings, EXPENDITURE summing final spending — and they must agree
Adding all bank deposits three ways

questions.question: Gross fixed capital formation is:
options: Spending that builds tomorrow's capacity — factories, roads and machines — the I in the expenditure method

questions.question: South Africa's structural shift means:
options: The primary sector now dominates GDP
The TERTIARY sector produces roughly two-thirds of GDP while manufacturing has stagnated — premature deindustrialisation
Mining has grown as a share of GDP

questions.question: Load-shedding is the case study proving that:
options: The tertiary sector needs no power
When the infrastructure SKELETON weakens, every sector limps — production cut, small firms closed, investment deterred

subtopics.title: Markets at Work — Elasticity, Costs and Revenue

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as:
options: Percentage change in QUANTITY DEMANDED divided by percentage change in PRICE
Change in price divided by change in income
Total revenue divided by total cost

questions.question: The chief determinant of elasticity is:
options: The AVAILABILITY OF SUBSTITUTES — plus necessity versus luxury, budget share, and time

questions.question: Facing INELASTIC demand, raising the price:
options: RAISES total revenue — the quantity lost is small, as with bread, petrol and electricity

questions.question: The profit-maximising rule for a price-taking firm is to produce where:
options: MARGINAL REVENUE EQUALS MARGINAL COST — before it each unit adds profit, beyond it each unit eats profit

subtopics.title: Connected Markets and the Two Policies

questions.question: When beef's price rises, the market for its substitute chicken sees:
options: Chicken's DEMAND CURVE shift RIGHT — buyers compare relative prices and switch
A movement along chicken's demand curve only

questions.question: "Every job hides inside something somebody buys" describes:
options: The PRODUCT-FACTOR loop — demand for labour is DERIVED from demand for products

questions.question: Raising the repo rate transmits to the economy as:
options: Banks raise prime, borrowing costs more, spending cools, inflation eases — at the cost of slower growth

questions.question: Monetary and fiscal policy differ in that:
options: Both are run by the Reserve Bank
The independent SARB moves the repo rate fast targeting inflation, while government's budget moves spending and taxes yearly targeting growth, jobs and redistribution

subtopics.title: Three Kitchens and Four Pay Packets

questions.question: In kitchen two, "the memo does not know what the till knows" means:
options: Planners lack the PRICE SIGNALS that reveal what people actually want — so shelves overflow beside shelves standing empty
Tills are illegal in planned economies

questions.question: The Sandton restaurant beside the paraffin-stove kitchen illustrates:
options: South Africa's DUAL economy — first-world and informal economies in one country

questions.question: Profit is "the only pay packet that can be empty" because:
options: It is the LEFTOVER after rent, wages and interest — sometimes nothing, sometimes negative — the price of carrying risk
It is paid first each month

subtopics.title: Rubber Bands, Planks and the Next Plate

questions.question: Bread demand is a PLANK because:
options: It has few substitutes, is a necessity, and takes a small budget slice — quantity barely bends when price moves

questions.question: Raising the price of a RUBBER BAND product:
options: EMPTIES the till — customers bounce away faster than the higher price compensates; the price CUT can fill it instead

questions.question: The kota stand's rent, owed even on a day with zero plates, is:
options: A FIXED cost — unchanged by output, unlike the bread and polony that walk out with every plate

questions.question: "Interrogate the next plate" means the stand should keep cooking while:
options: The NEXT plate costs LESS than the thirty rand it earns — and stop where the next one costs exactly what it earns

subtopics.title: The Till Slip and the Two Drivers

questions.question: The country's till slip can be added three ways that must agree:
options: What each business ADDED, what each factor EARNED, and what everyone SPENT

questions.question: The three departments of the slip are:
options: Out of the ground, through the factory, over the counter — primary, secondary, tertiary — with the counter now about two-thirds of the total

questions.question: Driver one's one-line job description is:
options: Keep INFLATION between three and six percent, using the repo rate pedal

questions.question: "Fast pedal, slow ship" contrasts:
options: The repo rate moving in an afternoon against the budget turning once a year — monetary speed against fiscal weight
